name: olai-plugin-claude
//name: UNSCOPED, like every other tenant: `@olai/*` is the scope for the packages that ARE olai, and an ENGINE is somebody else's agent with olai's judgement about it on top — the closest thing in this tree to a plugin written outside it. The directory is the plugin word (`claude`), which is the row's `id`, the word `--plugins` takes, and the address of its docs page.
//exports: FIVE, and the split is the tree's three-door rule with nothing added. `./server` is what the row mounts: the leg, the probe that finds this adapter on a host, and the install sentence — no `solid-js` anywhere on that graph, because a process that renders nothing must not pull a UI runtime. `./browser` is the chunk the tab fetches when the roster names this plugin, and it carries exactly one face: the mark this engine wears in a transcript's speaker column, which used to be a `MARKS` table inside `@olai/web` keyed by engine id. The ROOT is the wire identity and nothing more — this plugin composes no sibling surface, because an engine has nothing to publish that is not already on the chat cell. `./testids` and `./all.css` are the two contracts the generated bundle files need of every row.
//: THE CLAUDE CODE ENGINE — the leg that reads its wire, the two model bets its picker needs, the adapter olai ships pinned, and the mark it wears. One directory, one row, one release clock: this adapter's pin moved five times in a month and no other engine's did, which is the whole argument for a plugin per engine rather than one roster plugin.
//dependencies: `@olai/acp/engine` is the shape both ends spell — the leg, the adapter, the registration — and it is a floor package under both this plugin and `olai-plugin-chat`, which is what lets neither import the other. `@olai/plugin-api` is the door: the `Agents` tag its `./server` registers into, and the slot service its `./browser` hangs a mark in. `effect` because a plugin's `apply` is one. `solid-js` because the mark is a component.
//devDependencies: The protocol SDK for `PermissionOption`, in the leg's OWN bench alone: the leg itself names none of the SDK's types any more (`@olai/acp/engine` carries the ones a leg's signatures need), and the fixtures that stage a permission request do. Type-only, so no SDK code and no zod enter this package's closure — the claim `@olai/acp`'s manifest test makes about itself, kept here by the same instrument.
